covers: The sixteen registers of the AM9517A (8237A) DMA controller

entries.name: ch0 address
entries.description: Channel 0's address register, a 16-bit value reached a byte at a time.
entries.behaviour: A read returns the current address and a write sets the base and the current address, one byte at a time through the byte pointer flip-flop shared by every channel register: low byte first, then high.

entries.name: ch0 count
entries.description: Channel 0's word count register, a 16-bit value reached a byte at a time.
entries.behaviour: A read returns the current word count and a write sets the base and the current count, one byte at a time through the byte pointer flip-flop shared by every channel register: low byte first, then high.

sources.cites: Base and Current Word Count     Write

entries.name: status
entries.description: Status register, read: which channels reached terminal count and which have a request pending.
entries.behaviour: Bits 0 to 3 are set when a channel reaches terminal count and are cleared by the read; bits 4 to 7 are set while a channel's request is pending. MAME inverts bits 4 to 7 when the command register makes DREQ active low.

entries.name: command
entries.description: Command register, write: the controller-wide options.
entries.behaviour: Bit 0 enables memory-to-memory transfers, bit 1 holds channel 0's address, bit 2 disables the controller, bit 3 selects compressed timing, bit 4 rotating priority, bit 5 extended write, bit 6 makes DREQ active low, bit 7 makes DACK active high.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X ignores the command register ("Command reg not used"); MAME acts on its bits.

entries.name: request
entries.description: Request register, write: sets or clears a channel's software request.
entries.behaviour: Bits 1 and 0 select the channel and bit 2 sets (1) or clears (0) its request bit.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X does nothing with a write to it (a TODO); MAME sets or clears the channel's request bit.

sources.cites: case 0x9:		/* Request registers, memory to memory */

entries.name: single mask bit
entries.description: Single mask register, write: masks or unmasks one channel.
entries.behaviour: Bits 1 and 0 select the channel and bit 2 masks (1) or unmasks (0) it.

entries.name: mode
entries.description: Mode register, write: the transfer mode of the channel named in bits 1 and 0.
entries.behaviour: Bits 3 and 2 give the transfer (00 verify, 01 write, 10 read), bit 4 autoinitialize, bit 5 decrement the address, bits 7 and 6 the mode (00 demand, 01 single, 10 block, 11 cascade). MAME also clears that channel's terminal-count bit.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X keeps only autoinitialize, the direction and the transfer type; it takes no demand, single, block or cascade mode.

entries.name: clear byte pointer
entries.description: Software command, write: resets the byte pointer flip-flop so the next channel register access is a low byte.
entries.behaviour: Any write resets the flip-flop shared by every channel register. It must precede a new address or count.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X also resets the flip-flop on a read of this register; MAME has no read handler for it.

entries.name: master clear
entries.description: Software command, write: resets the controller as the hardware reset does.
entries.behaviour: Any write clears the command, status, request and temporary registers and the flip-flop, and sets the mask register.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X's master clear masks every channel and clears the terminal counts and the flip-flop; it leaves requests alone.

entries.name: temporary register
entries.description: Temporary register, read: the last byte moved by a memory-to-memory transfer.
entries.behaviour: A read returns the byte the last memory-to-memory transfer held.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X has no temporary register: a read logs an undefined port and returns all ones.

entries.name: clear mask
entries.description: Software command, write: unmasks all four channels.
entries.behaviour: Any write clears the mask bits of all four channels so they accept requests.

entries.name: write all mask bits
entries.description: Mask register, write: sets the mask bit of every channel at once.
entries.behaviour: Bits 0 to 3 are the mask bits of channels 0 to 3; a set bit masks the channel.

entries.name: mask readback
entries.description: Mask register, read: the mask bit of every channel.
entries.behaviour: A read returns the four mask bits, bit 0 for channel 0. A set bit means the channel is masked.
